shared_text:
The flight. A regional jet on a visual approach at night, in visual conditions.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and the captain the pilot monitoring.

What happened. On the base leg of the visual approach, the first officer had 2,100 ft set in the flight guidance panel and was descending slowly on the autopilot. During the turn onto final, the first officer chose to fly using the touch control steering override, and the aircraft lost altitude in the turn. When the aircraft was at 2,000 ft, the captain advised a correction and told the first officer to maintain 2,100 ft. Shortly afterwards the ground proximity warning system gave a terrain warning, and the captain called a go-around. At the lowest point, about 1,900 ft above sea level, the tower also issued a low altitude alert. The crew went around.
safe_outcome: ATC resequenced the aircraft. The second approach was stable and the aircraft landed normally. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: Another aircraft was climbing nearby. Both crews received TCAS resolution advisories and followed them, and the aircraft passed about 300 feet vertically and half a mile apart. A flight attendant on this aircraft was thrown against a galley cart during the manoeuvre and received a minor injury.

notes: Single narrative (captain, pilot monitoring). Rule 3, removed: the suggestion that the first officer's visual approach planning skills could be improved. 'Had good altitude set' rendered as the plain fact '2,100 ft set'. Rule 5, moved to the safe ending: the resequencing, stable second approach and landing. Rule 6: airport and runway removed. Judgement calls: 'chose to' is kept because it is the reporter's own description of the override. The clause explaining touch control steering is a definition of the system, not from the report, added so a reader unfamiliar with the type can follow; remove it if unwanted (the text would then be 143 words). Light is not coded; 'at night' is inferred from the coded local time (18:01-24:00, November).
